A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same divergence-estimation framework and KLDO method. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-divergence simulations and multi-model alignment experiments, including separation, AdvBench ASR, and AlpacaEval results.

after.justification: V2 retains original alignment experiments and adds adversarial, toxicity-classification, knowledge, reasoning, and PCA-variance results.

M1.justification: KLDO's objective and moving-average gradient estimator, and the general FDO construction, remain unchanged in Section 4.2. The added computational discussion does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V2 adds GCG-optimized AdvBench and SALAD transfer-attack scenarios, ToxiGen toxicity classification, and MMLU/GSM8K-CoT knowledge and reasoning evaluation. Existing CR/Pref training coverage and AlpacaEval evaluation remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DPO, KTO, BCO, and KLDO, with base-model references in separation and response illustrations. The added benchmarks reuse these alignment methods rather than introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: V2 removes silhouette scoring, introduces a standardized weighted robustness score and protocols for the added attack, classification, and exact-match evaluations, and normalizes correlation inputs within each model. Figure 1 also changes its illustrative model pairing. Appendix C's training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds optimized and transfer-attack robustness tests, PCA explained-variance analysis in Appendix C.4, and two response case studies in Tables 7–8. It retains the CR-versus-Pref analysis and latent-space illustrations but removes the silhouette-versus-ASR analysis.

E5.justification: Correlation estimation now normalizes both variables within each model before Pearson analysis. P-values and win-rate uncertainty displays already existed and remain. Neither version documents training seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2 and Figure 5 add extensive adversarial, toxicity, composite-robustness, knowledge, and reasoning results; Appendix C adds PCA and case-study outcomes. The Llama3.2-1B KLDO AdvBench entry changes from 10.77% to 4.81%, without explaining the revision. Correlation results are replaced under the revised normalization.

T1.justification: The divergence identities, alignment-consistency definition, Theorems 4.1/4.3/4.5, Lemma B.1, and Appendix A–B definitions and proofs retain their mathematical substance. Rewording and equation renumbering do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a divergence interpretation of alignment, KLDO/FDO construction, consistency-induced separation, benefits of CR data, and separation as a robustness indicator. V2 mainly supplies broader evidence and emphasizes KLDO as an application of the framework.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits experimental validation to models of at most 7B parameters, discusses reasoning applications and KLDO's resource efficiency, and explains robustness through harder transitions between representation clusters. V1's silhouette-versus-separation qualification is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix C clarifies that distance estimation uses the first two PCA components and adds KLDO cost discussion, while retaining training and hardware details. V1's concrete repository/dataset hyperlinks are absent in v2. The revised main-text response-generator description agrees with the Llama-3 source already documented in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for the new benchmarks and prompt-driven safeguarding, and removes several SFT-data and attack references. It broadens the discussion of representation-based attacks and defenses while retaining its divergence-based research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and substantial method/experiment explanations are rewritten or condensed. Related-work subsections are consolidated, and the conclusion becomes a Limitations and Future Work section.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text to one column, merges divergence plots, rebuilds robustness and correlation displays, and converts AlpacaEval and CR/Pref tables into charts. It adds benchmark/PCA/case-study displays and redraws, recolors, and redistributes the retained latent-space illustrations.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important validation gap by testing optimized and transfer jailbreaks beyond v1's AdvBench evaluation, and checking knowledge and reasoning utility beyond judged response preferences. These tests and the explicit model-size limitation substantially strengthen assessment of the safety–utility claims. Omitted access links and incomplete specification of the composite robustness score reduce reproducibility, but do not outweigh the stronger direct evidence.
